{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Clean revenue: remove commas and convert to float
df['revenue_clean'] = df['revenue'].str.replace(',', '', regex=False).astype(float)

# Identify and exclude QA test orders (revenue = 999999.99)
qa_mask = df['revenue_clean'] == 999999.99

# Identify and exclude refunded orders
refunded_mask = df['status'] == 'refunded'

# Define the final population: exclude QA and refunded orders
valid_mask = ~(qa_mask | refunded_mask)

# Filter to valid population
df_clean = df[valid_mask].copy()

# Check the number of rows after filtering
print(f'Number of QA test orders: {qa_mask.sum()}')
print(f'Number of refunded orders: {refunded_mask.sum()}')
print(f'Number of valid orders: {len(df_clean)}')

# Check distribution of channels and segments
print('\nChannel distribution:')
print(df_clean['channel'].value_counts())

print('\nCustomer segment distribution:')
print(df_clean['customer_segment'].value_counts())

# Check if channel and segment are confounded
print('\nCross-tabulation of channel and customer_segment:')
print(pd.crosstab(df_clean['channel'], df_clean['customer_segment']))"}
